title: Geometric flatness of algebraic spaces equals flatness of the ringed etale morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Z,W$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $h:Z\to W$ be any $S$-morphism. Let $(h^{-1},h_*,h^\sharp)$ be its canonical morphism of ringed small etale topoi [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], with $h^\sharp:h^{-1}\mathcal O_W\to\mathcal O_Z$. Then $h$ is flat on etale scheme charts if and only if $\mathcal O_Z$, regarded by $h^\sharp$ as an $h^{-1}\mathcal O_W$-module sheaf, is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Here flatness on charts means: for each etale scheme chart $V\to W$ and each etale scheme chart $T\to Z\times_W V$, the induced scheme morphism $T\to V$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Tag 073C (lemma-flat-morphism-sites), statement and proof; flatness on charts as in definition-P and lemma-flat-local.

proof.text: Put $R=h^{-1}\mathcal O_W$ and let $M=\mathcal O_Z$ with its $R$-action through $h^\sharp$. The ringed morphism is precisely the canonical one of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. For every geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$, put $\bar w=h\bar z$. By [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative], $(h^{-1}\mathcal O_W)_{\bar z}\cong\mathcal O_{W,\bar w}$, compatibly with algebraic operations and the map on stalk rings. Consequently $M_{\bar z}=\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$ has, under this identification, the scalar action given by the induced map $\mathcal O_{W,\bar w}\to\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$ of [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness]. Thus the stalk module uses the same ring homomorphism as the geometric flatness criterion.

The geometric points supplied by [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative] are points of the small etale topos and jointly detect isomorphisms. In the fixed small-site universes take representatives as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-conservative-flatness] on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ to this conservative family, to the ring sheaf $R$, and to the module $M$. By step 1 and [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $M$ is flat over $R$ if and only if every induced ring homomorphism $\mathcal O_{W,h\bar z}\to\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$ is flat. This application uses an arbitrary ring sheaf; it makes no assertion that $R$ is constant.

source.place: Tag 05VC (lemma-check-flat-stalks), applied as in spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073C (lemma-flat-morphism-sites).

proof.text: Assume flatness on the charts specified in the statement. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to W$, and a surjective etale scheme atlas $T\to Z\times_WV$, which exist by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $T\to Z$ is etale and surjective. For a geometric point $\bar z$ with image $z$, choose $t\in T$ over $z$. The scheme map $T\to V$ is flat by the chart hypothesis, hence flat at $t$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The compatible diagram $T\to V$ over $Z\to W$ therefore witnesses flatness of $h$ at $z$ in the precise sense of [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness]. That lemma implies that $\mathcal O_{W,h\bar z}\to\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$ is flat. Step 2 now proves flatness of $M$ over $R$.

Conversely assume $M$ flat over $R$. Take any etale scheme chart $V\to W$ and any etale scheme chart $T\to Z\times_WV$. These charts need not be surjective. The fibre-product and composition assertions of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] make $T\to Z$ etale, so $T\to V$ is a compatible etale chart diagram. For each $t\in T$, choose a geometric point $\bar t$ over $t$ and put $\bar z$ equal to its composite with $T\to Z$. Step 2 gives flatness of $\mathcal O_{W,h\bar z}\to\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$. By [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness], $h$ is flat at $z$, the image of $t$. Its explicit independence of the choices of compatible charts says that this may be tested in the present diagram at the present point $t$; hence $T\to V$ is flat at $t$. Since $t$ was arbitrary, [def-weil-flat-morphism] makes $T\to V$ flat. This proves the required universal chart condition. Empty charts have no points to test, so the argument includes the empty source.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q25-1f2356b28 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 073C, 04NG and 05VC (with the preceding lemma-stalk-flat) in full; every tag maps to the label cited. The item statement is unchanged from the base and matches 073C with the universal chart quantifier, so no target is weakened. There was no base proof and no re-split note. Step 1: the conservative-points node gives (h^{-1}F)_{z̄} ≅ F_{h z̄}, compatible with stalk ring maps and algebraic operations, so R_{z̄} ≅ O_{W,w̄} and M_{z̄} gets its scalar action through the strict-local stalk map. Step 2: the new 05VC node applied to the non-constant ring sheaf h^{-1}O_W, with def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, gives: M flat iff every stalk map O_{W,h z̄}→O_{Z,z̄} is flat. Step 3 is the 04NG argument: surjective atlases, fibre-product base change and composition of surjective étale maps make T→Z surjective étale, so T→V flat at t witnesses flatness at z. Step 4: base change of a non-surjective chart is étale by the stack-calculus base-change clause; I read the strict-local node's 'does not depend on the choices' as one diagram iff all, as in the 04NG proof, which gives T→V flat at every t. The empty source is vacuous on both sides. New node lem-sfb-ringed-site-conservative-flatness is self-contained, statement-only and matches 05VC; it holds for topos points because the forward direction holds for any ringed-topos morphism (lemma-pullback-flat). I tested it on a one-object site, M=0, a degenerate topos with an empty family and a non-constant R. It is not a duplicate of etale-flat-geometric-fibers (fixed constant ring), ringed-site-point-flat or pc-flat-sheaf-stalk-flat (forward direction only), and it is strictly smaller than the item. lean.note: Uses the existing chartwise MapIsFlat and canonical IsFlatEtaleRingedMap predicates.
